title: Ireland – Repair and maintenance services of electrical and mechanical building installations – Provision of Mechanical, Electrical, Instrumentation, Control, and Automation (MEICA) Support Services for Licensed Landfills in County Donegal.
description: Donegal County Council invites tenders from competent service providers for the provision of comprehensive Mechanical, Electrical, Instrumentation, Control, and Automation (MEICA) support services across six closed landfill facilities in County Donegal. The successful contractor will be required to deliver routine preventative maintenance, emergency fault diagnostics, 24/7/365 rapid response call-out interventions, and component updates on specialised environmental infrastructure. The scope of works includes troubleshooting industrial automation platforms, tuning SCADA/telemetry networks, field instrumentation calibrations (such as inline electromagnetic flow meters), electrofusion/butt welding on chemical pipework, and localised pump upkeep. Major capital replacement materials will typically be supplied by the Council for installation by the contractor. The contract will be established for an initial fixed term of one (1) year, with the unilateral option for Donegal County Council to extend the agreement for an additional period of up to one (1) year subject to performance and budget authorisation. Bids will be evaluated via a two-stage Open Procedure based on Pass/Fail suitability followed by Lowest Cost.

title: Labor Market Transparency & Fraud Detection Tools - RFI/Industry Day
description: 1. Purpose The U.S. Department of Labor (DOL) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 10, Market Research, to identify commercially available platforms that can support DOL�s efforts to improve labor market transparency, workforce identity verification, employment compliance, and detection of potential fraud and unlawful labor practices. The information received will assist the Government in understanding industry capabilities, refining requirements, assessing risks, and developing an appropriate acquisition strategy consistent with applicable procurement laws and regulations. This RFI is for planning and market research purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal, request for quote, or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any supplies or services. 2. Project Overview DOL is exploring commercially available digital workforce identity and compliance platforms that can provide secure, verifiable data to improve labor market transparency and identify indicators of potential fraud. Specifically, DOL seeks solutions offering trusted identity verification and work authorization status for workers, portable digital credentials (e.g., certifications, training and licensing records) that workers can share with employers or regulators, and electronic records of key compliance activities (such as wage payments, safety training completion, housing and transportation inspections, and worksite assignments) to support employers in meeting labor standards. The ideal platform will generate audit-ready logs and reports of employment and compliance data, use data analytics to flag potential fraud, document inconsistencies, or unlawful labor practices, and support greater transparency in the workforce (for example, by confirming that workers are deployed as authorized and that required conditions are being upheld). Importantly, any solution must incorporate privacy and security by design, obtain appropriate consent for personal data use, and complement existing legal employment verification and worker protection processes. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 513210 (Software Publishers). 3. Requested Information DOL requests that interested parties address the following areas: A. Company Information Company name, address, and point of contact Business size and socioeconomic status (e.g., small business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB) Relevant NAICS codes Primary point of contact Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Applicable contract vehicles that the solution is available (if any) B. Relevant Experience Description of experience providing labor market transparency and fraud detection tools Experience working with federal agencies Examples of similar projects/contracts completed within the last 5 � 7 years C. Technical Capabilities and Anticipated Approach Capabilities related to providing labor market transparency and fraud detection tools How does your solution differentiate itself from alternative options on the market? Does your solution include artificial intelligence? If yes, to what extent? What reporting, analytics, or data insights will your platform provide, and how often? What is the estimated timeline to fully deploy this solution? What kind of initial and ongoing training or support do you provide to clients? How is cybersecurity addressed for the solution? D. Cost Considerations Please provide a high-level, Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) for your solution. Describe the pricing model, such as a subscription, user-based, usage-based, etc. What are the major cost drivers? Is the proposed solution available through an existing Government-wide acquisition contract? 4. Industry Day DOL intends to host an Industry Day to provide interested vendors with an opportunity to demonstrate their relevant capabilities. Tentative Date: September 24 - 25, 2026 Location: Virtual Format: Presentation and demo via MS Teams DOL may request vendors to demonstrate one or more of the following conditions within their solution: A. Worker Identity How a worker establishes and maintains a trusted digital identity and how an authorized employer or Government user verifies the identity. B. Digital Credentials How a worker receives, maintains, and securely shares a digital certification or safety-training credential and how an authorized party validates the credential. C. Compliance How employment and compliance information, such as wage payments, training completion, worksite assignments, or inspection records, is collected and maintained. D. Fraud Detection How the platform identifies an inconsistency or anomalous pattern across multiple records and generates an alert or risk indicator for further human review. E. Investigation and Audit How an authorized DOL user examines supporting information, identifies the source of the underlying data, and generates an audit-ready report. F. Privacy and Security How the platform manages consent, user access, data sharing, privacy controls, security controls, and audit logs. Vendors should be prepared to identify which capabilities demonstrated are currently commercially available, which are configurable, and which would require customization or new development. DOL requests that respondents address the following questions during Industry Day, as applicable: What data sources are required to operate the solution effectively? What sources can the solution access or integrate with? What information (if any) should be collected directly from workers, employers, Government agencies, or other sources? What are the primary privacy risks associated with a digital workforce identity platform? How can DOL minimize collection and retention of unnecessary personal information? How should human review be incorporated into fraud detection and compliance workflows? What steps are taken to minimize false positives? What interoperability standards should DOL consider? What integration challenges should DOL anticipate? What is a reasonable implementation timeline for a solution of this nature? What level of Government involvement is typically required during implementation? What is the general period of performance on contracts for your solution? What performance metrics should DOL consider when evaluating such a solution? Pick one fraud/compliance alert in the demo and walk us from the alert all the way back to every underlying data element. Which data came from the worker, employer, government, third party, or the platform itself? Which data are verified versus self-reported? Show us an employer trying to game the system What does the investigator actually receive? Can workers/employers record events without connectivity? How are timestamps and integrity preserved? How are conflicting offline records reconciled later? Can DOL export its data, schemas, audit logs and reports in usable nonproprietary formats? What happens to credentials issued to workers? What happens if the vendor fails, is acquired, or DOL changes providers? What are the five failure modes and which party controls each one: vendor, DOL, another federal agency, state, employer, or worker Which visa programs do they leverage / work with? Please expressly address credential expiration Who owns the data? Can the data be repurposed and, if so, under what conditions? 5. Industry Day Submission Interested vendors shall submit their responses by 10:00am (EST) on 9/17/2026 to Contracting Officer (CO) Broderick Morris at Morris.Broderick@dol.gov. Registration is required to attend the industry day. Attendees shall provide the following information with their email to Broderick Morris: Subject Line: RSVP Industry Day � DOL Labor Market Transparency & Fraud Detection Tools Company Name and Business Size (Include applicable socio-economic status) Name of Attendee(s) Attendee(s) Contact Information (Email and Phone N

title: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE / NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD ON A NONCOMPETITIVE BASIS
description: 1. Description of Requirement The 166th Airlift Wing, Delaware Air National Guard, intends to issue a firm-fixed-price task order on a noncompetitive basis to Veteran Equipment Sales LLC (VES), the manufacturer of the Government-furnished equipment (GFE), for the installation, integration, testing, startup, training, and commissioning services of a GFE VES heated semi down-draft aircraft paint booth system with attached mixing room at the Nose Dock Repair Facility. Additionally, as an option line item, funding dependent, the contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, transportation, tools, equipment, materials, supplies, factory-certified personnel, and incidental services necessary to install, integrate, test, startup, train Government personnel, and commission a Government-furnished VES NIOSH-Compliant Personnel Air Shower. The Government-furnished equipment includes: VES Personnel Air Shower: VES Part Number 965-100-001, National Stock Number 4460-01-698-7874 VES Paint Booth System: VES Part Number PB-100-000, National Stock Number 4940-01-707-5264 The Government is currently constructing a new fuel cell to house the equipment. Consequently, the contractor's installation schedule may be dependent upon the progress and completion of the Government's construction activities. 2. Manufacturer Certification and Warranty Requirements VES has advised the Government that third-party installers may perform installation only if the installers have been factory-trained and certified by VES prior to performing installation work. Each certified individual must possess written certification signed by the President of VES confirming the individual's qualification. VES further requires that, regardless of the installer's certification status, a VES factory-trained and certified field engineer must be present on site to supervise installation and perform startup and training in order to maintain the manufacturer's warranty. Because the requirement involves installation, integration, testing, startup, training, and commissioning of VES-manufactured equipment, the Government must ensure that the contractor can satisfy all applicable VES factory-certification, supervision, startup, training, and warranty requirements. 3. Intent and Capability Submission Instructions Based on the information presently available to the Government, VES is the intended source for this requirement. However, the Government is seeking information from other responsible sources to determine whether there are qualified sources capable of performing the complete requirement while satisfying the manufacturer's requirements. Interested sources are invited to submit information demonstrating their capability to perform the complete requirement. Responses from sources other than VES shall provide sufficient information for the Contracting Officer to determine whether the respondent can satisfy all requirements. At a minimum, respondents should identify: Their relationship or authorization status with VES Their ability to provide VES factory-trained and certified personnel to perform the installation Documentation demonstrating applicable VES factory certification signed by the President of VES Their ability to provide or coordinate the required VES factory-trained and certified field engineer to supervise installation and perform startup and training Their ability to install, integrate, test, start up, training Goverment personnel, and commission the Government-furnished VES equipment Their ability to satisfy all applicable VES manufacturer requirements necessary to maintain the equipment and equipment warranty Responses should clearly demonstrate the ability to perform the entire scope of work, including all required labor, supervision, transportation, tools, equipment, materials, supplies, factory-certified personnel, and incidental services. 4. Submission Deadline and Point of Contact Responses must be recieved no later than 17 September 2026, at 10:00 a.m. EST. Please submit all responses via email to Ms. Katesha Tolson at katesha.tolson.1@us.af.mil 5. Notice Disclaimer This notice is not a request for quotations or a solicitation. The Government will consider infromation received from responsible sources in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy.

title: Urgent UPS Maintenance Repair
description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT This notice is issued in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) section 5.201 to notify the public of a proposed contract action. The North American Identification Classification System (NAICS) code is 811210 Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance . The SBA size standard is f $34 million in average annual receipt. The proposed contract action is for a modification to an exisiting contract under which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 6.302(c)(1). The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C.253(c)(1) as implemented by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 6.302-1 entitled �3304(a)(1) sole source specifications, which reads in part, �Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.� The U.S Agency of Global Marketing (USAGM) intends to modify contract no. 951700-21-F-0193 awarded to Tower Facilities Management, LLC (Tower FM) for replacement, repair and maintnenance of our Uninterupted Power Supply (UPS) systems manufactured by General Electric, due to an urgent requirement for UPS replancement and repair. The mission critical requirement is necessary to provide back-up power to the building should an unforeseeable power outage occur. If power to the building fails, there would be operational delays due to system disruptions. The Voice of America (VOA) and United States Agency for Global Media (USAGM) have an immediate and most urgent requirement to procure certified General Electric (GE) manufacture technicians to provide maitnenace services to replace 2 Module Inv/Rectifier, 1 module Booster and 1 Bridge Can Bus Cable necessary for the repair of UPS#2 located int the UPS Room Garage Level 330 Independence Avenue, Washington, DC, 20237. This UPS repair will provide back-up power for our critical infrastructure to the building needed to support the agncey's mission. Tower FM is the only contractor known to immediate respond to this emergency and perform repairs on the General Electric (GE) Uninterrupted Power Supply (UPS) systems supporting this requirement. Tower FM maintains proprietary rights and access necessary to service GE UPS equipment, and its technicians possess specialized factory training that uniquely qualifies them to diagnose, repair, maintain, and provide technical recommendations for these systems with in 48 hours. Due to its exclusive authorization and specialized expertise, Tower FM is capable of ensuring repairs are performed in accordance with GE manufacturer's specifications and operational requirements. Utilizing Tower FM minimizes operational risk, supports system reliability, and helps ensure continued performance of critical power infrastructure. No other known source can provide the same level of authorized support, proprietary knowledge, and factory-trained technical services required for these GE UPS systems within the required timeframe. Estimated modification Value: $82,024.00 The only acceptable vendor for this service is: Tower Facilities Management, LLC Dustin Kominoth Pres./CEO 7226 Lee Deforest Drive Suite 105 Columbia, MD 21046 Phone 410.379.0080 Fax 410.379.0060 E-Mail DKominoth@Tower-FM.com This notice of intent is not a request for capability statements or competitive proposals; however all capability statements received within fifteen (15) days of the issuance of this notice will be considered by the agency. A determination by the Government not to compete this procurement based on responses to this notice is solely at the discretion of the Government. For questions concerning this notice, please contact Nicole Wright; email NWright@usagm.gov. or Natalie Y. Ellis; email: Nellis@usagm.gov

description: This requirement is to provide AV Support Services to the MARSOC G6. Per page 30 of the RFP A. The Government is not responsible for any vendor's failure to gain base entry in time for the site visit. E. Proposal Submission Proposals shall be received no later than 10:00AM EST on Sep 17, 2026. The minimum guarantee for this contract is established at $2,500.00, which shall be satisfied via the simultaneous issuance of the initial Task Order(s) at the time of base contract award. title: Request For Information (RFI) Web Based Respirator Medical Questionnaire & Evaluation Tool
description: Web-Based Respirator Medical Questionnaire and Evaluation Tool I. Introductory This is a Request for Information. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this Request for Information is to obtain details, capabilities and clarification from potential suppliers and knowledge and information on potential vendor interest for project planning purposes. II. Project Description Background Federal Occupational Health (FOH), a component of the Program Support Center (PSC) within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), provides occupational health services to more than 360 federal agencies and supports approximately 1.8 million federal employees throughout the United States, U.S. Territories, and internationally. As part of these services, FOH administers respirator medical evaluation and clearance services to assist customer agencies in complying with the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Respiratory Protection Standard (29 CFR 1910.134). FOH currently utilizes a web-based Respirator Medical Questionnaire and Evaluation Tool to support respirator medical evaluation and clearance activities. As the current contractual arrangement approaches its conclusion and the Government's cybersecurity, identity management, and operational requirements continue to evolve, FOH is conducting market research to identify vendors capable of providing, configuring, or developing a web-based Respirator Medical Questionnaire and Evaluation Tool that satisfies the Government's functional, clinical, operational, cybersecurity, privacy, accessibility, and identity management requirements. Information obtained through this Request for Information (RFI) will assist the Government in determining available commercial capabilities, implementation approaches, technical maturity, and acquisition strategies for this requirement. Purpose and Objectives The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to conduct market research to identify qualified vendors capable of providing, configuring, or developing a secure, web-based Respirator Medical Questionnaire and Evaluation Tool that satisfies the Government's requirements. The Government is seeking information regarding commercially available products, configurable commercial platforms, or custom-developed solutions capable of supporting OSHA-compliant respirator medical questionnaire and evaluation clearance processes while meeting the Government's functional, clinical, operational, cybersecurity, privacy, accessibility, and identity management requirements. The Government is particularly interested in determining whether industry currently offers solutions that satisfy these requirements through existing commercial capabilities, configurable platforms, or whether custom software development would be required. Specifically, the Government seeks information regarding industry's capability to provide solutions that: Support OSHA-compliant respirator medical questionnaire and evaluation clearance processes in accordance with OSHA Respiratory Protection Standard (29 CFR 1910.134). Provide automated questionnaire evaluation using configurable clinical decision logic to determine medical clearance or referral for further medical evaluation. Support physician review and follow-up medical evaluation processes performed by board-certified occupational medicine physicians. Provide secure electronic submission, storage, and review of follow-up medical documentation. Support user notification, medical clearance status tracking, reporting, and administrative case management. Support multiple federal customer agencies through configurable role-based administrative capabilities. Support SAML 2.0 or OpenID for integration with the Government's identity management environment. Implement phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication (MFA) for both internal government users and external customers in accordance with applicable federal cybersecurity requirements and guidance. Comply with applicable federal cybersecurity, privacy, records management, and Section 508 accessibility requirements. Support implementation within a federal environment requiring compliance with applicable HHS security requirements and an Authority to Operate (ATO), as applicable. The Government intends to use information obtained through this RFI to: Determine whether the Government's requirements can be satisfied through existing commercial capabilities, configurable commercial platforms, or custom-developed solutions. Assess the maturity of available commercial capabilities. Identify qualified vendors capable of satisfying the Government's requirements. Better understand implementation approaches, technical risks, and available commercial capabilities. Refine the Government's acquisition strategy and support development of any future solicitation. Anticipated Period of Performance The anticipated Period of Performance for this Solicitation is: Contract Period Period of Performance Base Period October 31, 2027 to October 30, 2028 Period 1 October 31, 2028 to October 30, 2029 Period 2 October 31, 2029 to October 30, 2030 Period 3 October 31, 2030 to October 30, 2031 Period 4 October 31, 2031 to October 30, 2032 Project Requirements The Government is seeking information regarding solutions capable of satisfying the functional, clinical, operational, cybersecurity, privacy, accessibility, and identity management requirements described in the Government's accompanying requirements documentation. The desired solution should include, but is not limited to, the capability to: Provide a secure, web-based Respirator Medical Questionnaire and Evaluation Tool that supports OSHA respirator medical evaluation and clearance requirements. Utilize automated questionnaire evaluation and configurable clinical decision logic to identify individuals who may be medically cleared or referred for further medical evaluation. Support medical review and follow-up evaluation processes performed by board-certified occupational medicine physicians. Support secure electronic submission, storage, and review of follow-up medical documentation. Notify users of medical clearance status and required follow-up actions. Provide role-based access for employees, customer agency administrators, FOH personnel, and authorized medical reviewers. Support reporting, case management, and administrative oversight across multiple customer agencies. Support SAML 2.0 or OpenID for integration with the Government's identity management environment. Implement phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication (MFA) for both internal government users and external customers. Comply with applicable HHS cybersecurity, privacy, records management, and Section 508 accessibility requirements. Support implementation within a federal environment requiring compliance with applicable HHS security requirements and an Authority to Operate (ATO), as applicable. Respondents are encouraged to review the Government's accompanying requirements documentation and describe how their proposed solution satisfies the identified requirements. III. Disclaimer and Important Notes This notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract or otherwise pay for the information provided in response. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by the respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed. Information provided will be used to assess tradeoffs and alternatives available for the potential requirement and may lead to the development of a solicitation. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. description: Molaga Honey Ltd invites tenders for the supply, installation, delivery, and commissioning of machinery to support automation in a food production environment. This project aims to improve efficiency, hygiene standards, and production through integration of key automated equipment. Equipment includes: An Automatic Capper, capable of capping both jars and squeezies. This machine should have linear height control, so that we can adjust the height for jars and squeezies. An automated inline heat sealer system for high-volume production. Heat sealing creates airtight barriers, preventing oxygen, moisture, and contaminants from compromising our honey products in squeezy bottles. For Molaga Honey Ltd, this means there are fewer product returns, lower waste costs, and improved stock rotation flexibility. All equipment must be suitable for food-grade, high-care environments, constructed primarily of stainless steel, and compliant with relevant EU food safety and CE machinery regulations. Suppliers must provide full installation, commissioning, and operator training. Tenders will be evaluated on expertise, technical compliance, lead time, warranty terms, and overall value for money.

title: Human Hindbrain Organoid Functional Assay Services.
description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER), Division of Applied Regulatory Science (DARS), intends to award a sole-source, Firm-Fixed-Price purchase order to OrganoTherapeutics SARL for Human iPSC-Derived Hindbrain Organoid Functional Assay Services. The requirement includes the provision of human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived hindbrain organoids and associated materials necessary to support in vitro research evaluating drug-induced effects on respiratory-relevant neural circuits. The contractor will also perform functional characterization of the organoids using three-dimensional multi-electrode array (3D MEA) technology to assess electrophysiological responses to drugs known to affect respiratory function. The functional characterization includes testing FDA-identified drug and reversal-agent combinations, MEA measurements, evaluation of batch-to-batch reproducibility, collection of exposed drug solutions for FDA verification, data analysis, and delivery of raw data, analyzed data, analysis files, and study reports. The requirement also includes twelve scheduled deliveries of human hindbrain organoids to the FDA White Oak Campus. The first delivery will consist of 96 organoids, with subsequent deliveries consisting of 48 organoids each. Functional characterization will be performed at the contractor's laboratory. The anticipated period of performance is eighteen (18) months from the date of award. This acquisition is being conducted as a commercial service acquisition under RFO FAR Part 12. The Government's decision to restrict competition is documented pursuant to RFO FAR 12.102(a). Market research identified OrganoTherapeutics SARL as the only source capable of satisfying the Government's complete requirement for both the required human hindbrain organoids and associated functional assay services. This notice is not intended to restrict consideration of any responsible source capable of meeting the Government's complete requirement. All responsible sources may submit a quotation and supporting capability information by the response date identified in this notice. Any timely response demonstrating the capability to satisfy the Government's complete requirement will be considered by the Contracting Officer prior to award. NAICS: 541714 PSC: B504 � Special Studies/Analysis � Chemical/Biological Place of Delivery: FDA White Oak Campus, Silver Spring, Maryland Place of Service Performance: Contractor's laboratory

title: France – Exhibition centre construction work – Concession de service public pour l’exploitation du centre de congrès et parc d’expositions « Mégacité » et la réalisation de travaux d’extension et de rénovation
description: Implanté sur 35 000 m², MEGACITE est un pôle évènementiel qui permet l’organisation en intérieur et en extérieur de manifestations de type salons, congrès, séminaires, expositions, spectacles, etc. Construit en 1984, une extension du bâtiment a été réalisée en 2006. Il comprend principalement un ensemble d’espaces composé d’un amphithéâtre de 986 places, 4 halls d’expositions de 3800 m², 2400 m², 1800 m² et 1135 m², un espace polyvalent d’accueil de 600 m², 7 salles d’atelier de 30 à 300 personnes, un bar, des cuisines, des aires extérieures permettant l’implantation de chapiteaux. L’extension ouverte en 2006 comprend un amphithéâtre supplémentaire de 350 places, 2 salles d’atelier (70 et 90 places), une salle de presse, un espace de bureau dédié aux organisateurs. Compte tenu de l’état du site, le prochain contrat mettra à la charge du concessionnaire la construction d’une halle modulaire de 5000 à 8000 m² destinée aux foires, salons, expositions et congrès comprenant un office restauration ainsi que la rénovation des espaces actuels. Le coût du projet est estimé entre 18 et 23,5 M€TTC. La construction de cette halle modulaire impliquera la démolition et le réaménagement d’une partie des infrastructures qui feront l’objet de travaux pris en charge par Amiens Métropole qui auront lieu après 2032. Enfin, l’exploitation des espaces mutualisés du Quai de l’innovation sera intégrée en option dans le périmètre de la concession. Cet équipement est situé au cœur du quartier historique St Leu et comporte des espaces mutualisés représentant environ 1 900 m² incluant des salles de réunions, des salles de conférence gradinées de 50 à 300 places ainsi que des espaces de bureau, de réception, de coworking et de visio-conférence. Durée du contrat La durée de 180 mois est la durée minimum du contrat. Selon les projets des candidats et l’économie générale des offres, cette durée pourra être portée à 240 mois maximum. Conditions d’exécution de la concession Le concessionnaire percevra directement les recettes d’exploitation et supportera directement les charges du service sur la durée du contrat. Amiens Métropole versera une subvention d’investissement plafonnée à 70% du coût total des investissements. Le cas échéant, la collectivité versera au concessionnaire une contribution financière afin de prendre en compte le niveau des missions de service public qu'elle entend lui imposer Par ailleurs, la convention prévoira les modalités d’un intéressement dans l’hypothèse où le résultat dégagé par le concessionnaire serait supérieur à ses prévisions. Informations complémentaires La description des prestations ainsi que la liste des pièces à fournir par les candidats figurent dans la pièce intitulée "Informations complémentaires candidats Mégacité".

title: The National ALS Registry Expansion of Outreach and Awareness to Persons with ALS in Select States Covered by the Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) Association
description: The Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry (ATSDR) intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract to the Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) Association for the project titled "The National ALS Registry Expansion of Outreach and Awareness to Persons with ALS in Select States covered by the ALS Association." The contract will promote and enroll patients into the National ALS (Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis) Registry by providing continuous outreach, education, awareness (e.g., facilitate ALS patient computer access to the National ALS Registry web portal; provide educational materials; use social media, etc.) to persons with ALS, their families, caregivers, and researchers. These activities will be directed in the states of: Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, California � Sacramento Area, Florida, Idaho, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Vermont, Virginia, West Virginia, and Wisconsin. The ALS Association is uniquely qualified to fulfill this requirement because it possesses a combination of national ALS clinical infrastructure, credentialing authority, research engagement, and established patient and provider relationships that is not available from any other organization. This contract action is for services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of RFO FAR 6.103-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements, and is justified under 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1). This notice of intent to sole source is not a request for competitive quotations; however, all quotations/responses received within 15 of days of the issuance of this notice shall be considered by the government. A determination by the government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Any quotation/response should be emailed to uwo8@cdc.gov by the posted deadline.

REQUIREMENT Parks Canada Agency (PCA) has a requirement for a Contractor to perform the renewal of the exterior. The objective of this project is to establish a secure building envelop resistance to the environment. TWO-SUBMISSION BID This Bid shall be submitted following a “two-submission” procedure. Refer to SI04 of the Special Instructions to Bidders. This Invitation to Tender contains bid criteria in order to provide socioeconomic benefits to Indigenous communities within the area covered by the contract. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE Contractor shall perform and complete the Work no later than November 1, 2026. Arrangements have been made for the site visit to be held at the Firehall - 207 Fountain Avenue, Waterton Park, Alberta. on September 8, 2026. The site visit will begin 1:00 PM (MDT-HAR). INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. title: Netherlands – Winter-maintenance materials – Inkoop advies en materieel gladheidsbestrijding
description: De scope van de opdracht is het samen met de opdrachtgever voorbereiden van de gladheidsbestrijding, het leveren en onderhouden van het benodigd materieel en materiaal voor de gladheidsbestrijding en het ondersteunen bij de uitvoering van de gladheidsbestrijding. Om een versnipperde inkoop te voorkomen is gekozen voor een opgavegerichte aanpak. Buiten deze inkoop vallen: o Het leveren van zout en pekel; o Het coördineren en uitvoeren van gladheidsbestrijding; o Het beheer en onderhoud van de gemeentelijke wegdekmeetpunten; o Het leveren van Meteorologische ondersteuning. - Een nieuw gladheidsbestrijdingsplan (beleid en operationeel) opstellen en implementeren; - Levering/huur/lease etc. van vervangende wintermachines: gemeentelijke vloot van wintermachines actueel houden (operationeel, bedrijfszeker); - Routebegeleidingssystemen en voertuigtracking: implementeren, efficiënt en operationeel houden; - Kennisniveau medewerkers op peil brengen en houden; - Innovaties toepassen (aanjagen en benutten), opgaven zo duurzaam mogelijk invullen; - In samenwerking op een duurzame en integrale manier de gladheidsbestrijding jaarlijks realiseren; - Het realiseren van de duurzaamheidsopgave: 50% minder CO2 uitstoot en 50% circulair handelen in 2030; - Het maken van de aanzet richting de duurzaamheidsopgave: volledig klimaatneutraal en circulair handelen in 2050.

description: La présente consultation a pour objet la fourniture, le déploiement, l’hébergement et la maintenance d’une solution de gestion des marchés publics en mode SaaS pour la Ville de Marseille. La solution devra permettre de gérer l’ensemble du cycle de vie des marchés publics, de la préparation des procédures au suivi de leur exécution, en garantissant l’interopérabilité avec les outils existants de la collectivité, la traçabilité des actions et la simplification des processus de gestion. Le titulaire assurera également les prestations d’accompagnement au déploiement, de formation des utilisateurs, de support technique ainsi que la maintenance corrective et évolutive de la solution

title: Ireland – Library, archives, museums and other cultural services – Archaeological Processing and Archive Services for Accession and Storage in the National Museum of Ireland
description: Archaeological Processing and Archive Services for Accession and Storage in the National Museum of Ireland. The National Museum of Ireland requires archaeological processing services to; Sort, pack, document and prepare assemblages from a range of excavated or stored archaeological collections for storage/accession in the National Museum of Ireland to the contract specification and standards listed below. Contractors should demonstrate that they can provide a minimum of 1 supervisor archaeologist and 2 archaeological assistants (see definition and experience in Appendix A). A typical project of this type would have a minimum duration of at least 6 months. Sort, pack, document and transfer archaeological and other museum related archives, documents and reports in and/from a range of storage locations as outlined below. Contractors should demonstrate that they will be able to provide a minimum of 1 Archivist (see definition and experience in Appendix A). A typical work package could range from 6 months to a year. Provide services to wash, dry, process, pack and deliver osteological analysis and reporting to required standards (listed below) on assemblages of human remains of varying sizes including selection of samples for C14, Isotope and/or other analyses where recommended (varying sizes here could range from single bones to individual burials to large assemblages of articulated or disarticulated remains). A minimum requirement for a contract would be 1 Senior Osteoarchaeologist (see definition and experience in Appendix A) and the contractor should include an additional minimum of 2 Osteoarchaeologists for larger assemblages.

title: 140-ton 10-foot Hydraulic Press Brake
description: CLIN 0001: 140�150 Ton Industrial CNC Hydraulic Press Brake Quantity: 1 EA Pricing Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Item Description: The Contractor shall furnish and deliver one (1) new (not refurbished or prototype) Industrial CNC Hydraulic Press Brake meeting the following minimum salient characteristics: Tonnage Capacity: 140 to 150 Tons of hydraulic bending force. Bending Bed Length: Minimum 120 inches (10-foot) total usable working length. Cannot exceed 10-feet working width Clearance Between Side Frames: Minimum 100 inches internal clearance to accommodate standard sheet widths. Physical Footprint Envelope: Total assembled machine footprint shall not exceed 156 inches (13 feet) in width. Electrical / Motor Limits: Please state the Amperage, Voltage, and Motor HP to determine the electrical requirements. Frame & Weight: Minimum net machine weight of 14,000 lbs constructed from fully welded, stress-relieved structural steel. Control System: Integrated 2-Axis CNC Controller capable of storing a minimum of 40 unique programs with programmable back-gauge positioning and bend sequence angles. Tooling & Safety: Includes a standard Gooseneck punch, multi-V bottom die set with quick-release clamping, dual foot-pedal controls, and an ANSI/OSHA-compliant integrated optical light-curtain safety system. Trade Compliance: Must be manufactured in the United States, a DFARS Qualifying Country (DFARS 225.872-1), or a Trade Agreements Act (TAA) compliant country. CLIN 0002: Turnkey Logistics, Rigging, Commissioning, & Training Quantity: 1 Job (JB) Pricing Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Item Description: The Contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, specialized equipment, transportation, and rigging necessary to perform complete delivery, inside placement, mechanical setup, and operational verification of the equipment provided under CLIN 0001: Freight & Delivery (F.O.B. Destination): Transport machinery to the designated government facility delivery address with liftgate or dedicated flatbed coordination. Offloading & Heavy Rigging: Provide certified heavy machinery riggers, skates, and forklift/crane equipment capable of safely offloading the ~14,000�16,000 lb machine, transporting it through facility doorways/bays, and placing it onto the designated workshop concrete slab without damaging facility infrastructure. Mechanical Leveling & Anchoring: Level the machine to manufacturer tolerances and anchor/secure the chassis to the concrete floor per standard engineering safety guidelines. (Note: Facility electrical wiring up to the disconnect box to be provided by the Government; final hookup coordination by Contractor). Hydraulic Fluid & Commissioning: Fill the hydraulic reservoir with appropriate industrial-grade hydraulic fluid, verify pump pressures, test emergency stop/light-curtain systems, and perform a live test bend on government-furnished material to verify 2-axis CNC repeatability. On-Site Operator Training: Provide a minimum of four (4) to eight (8) hours of comprehensive on-site operator training for up to four (4) government personnel, covering machine startup, CNC programming, tool changes, basic maintenance procedures, and safety protocols.

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Dormitory Wi-Fi
description: The 5th Contracting Squadron (5 CONS) at Minot Air Force Base (MAFB), ND, intends to negotiate and award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price commercial contract to SRT Communications, Inc. (3615 N Broadway, Minot, ND 58703) for Dormitory High-Speed Internet and Wi-Fi Services across Minot AFB. This acquisition is being conducted under the authority, as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation FAR Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services). The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 517112 (Wired Telecommunications Carriers). SRT Communications, Inc. is the only known source capable of fulfilling this requirement without causing unacceptable, mission-degrading operational delays and substantial, non-recoverable duplication of government costs. SRT Communications, Inc. owns and operates the existing, proprietary fiber-optic infrastructure, including in-unit media centers, Wi-Fi routers, fiber jumpers, and outside plant fiber leading to dormitory demarcation points on MAFB. Awarding to any other vendor would require a complete teardown and replacement of the existing network infrastructure, creating severe service disruptions for resident Airmen and significant, redundant costs to the Government. title: Program Manager, Intelligence and Cyberspace Operations Maritime Targeting Cell Shelter Systems
description: General Announcement THIS NOTICE OF INTENT/SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATION PURPOSES ONLY. Program Manager, Intelligence and Cyberspace Operations (PM ICO) within Portfolio Acquisition Executive � Marine Corps (PAE-MC) provides this sources sought and notice of intent to award on a sole-source basis in accordance with 10 United States Code (U.S.C.) �3204 (a)(1), as implemented by the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-1(b) to Anduril Industries Inc., 1400 Anduril, Costa Mesa CA 92626-1548, CAGE: 85LD7, Unique Entity Identifier: KC3CH2MSK7Q3. The PMICO has a requirement for the procurement of fifteen (15) Maritime Targeting Cell (MTC) Shelter Systems, comprising (8) eight Operator Shelters and seven (7) Processing Shelters. These highly specialized, expeditionary, road-transportable, dual-shelter systems are required to support the urgent operational imperatives and timelines of the MTC program. These systems will provide a secure, self-contained, and ruggedized operating environment for conducting sensitive intelligence operations in contested and austere forward-deployed environments. 2. Basis for Sole-Source Justification Comprehensive market research was conducted across industry, including the evaluation of various vendor capability statements submitted in response to a previously posted Request for Information. Based on the responses received and technical analysis of market capabilities, the following was determined: Intended Source & Lack of Competition: Anduril Industries Inc. (1400 Anduril, Costa Mesa CA 92626-1548) is the only known source capable of satisfying the Government�s urgent operational requirements without unacceptable technical risk, cost duplication, and schedule delay. Competition is lacking because no other vendor possesses a mature, field-tested production configuration that provides turnkey integration with the Government-specified MEP-1070 generator set while concurrently meeting all expeditionary physical footprint, modularity, road-transportability, and operational security parameters. Technical & Integrated Architecture: The proprietary baseline developed by Anduril Industries provides pre-engineered structural, environmental, and tactical power integration with the required MEP-1070 generator set. This turnkey architecture is critical to minimizing the logistical footprint, ensuring rapid deployment, and significantly reducing setup time in austere, forward-operating environments. Programmatic & Schedule Impact: Alternative vendor concepts reviewed during market research would require extensive re-engineering, power integration/distribution redesign, and developmental qualification, to include environmental and flight/road-transport certifications. Pursuing an alternative development effort would introduce programmatic delays, creating an unacceptable operational gap in meeting mission-critical fleet deployment timelines for the MTC program. The Government anticipates award of a Firm-Fixed-Price delivery order, with a period of performance of approximately two (2) years. In tandem with executing this sole-source action and for all future opportunities, PM ICO will continue to conduct market research, monitor emerging industry capabilities, and actively pursue competitive acquisition strategies to the greatest extent practicable for future MTC program lifecycle and follow-on requirements. 3. Capability Statement Submission Instructions THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS OR QUOTATIONS. However, all responsible sources may submit a technical capability statement, proposal, or quotation demonstrating their ability to satisfy the Government's operational and technical requirements. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 7F20, IT and Telecom � IT Management Tool/Products (Hardware and Perpetual License Software). title: Wearable Safety & Physiological Monitoring Technology
description: THIS IS NOT A NOTICE OF SOLICITATION ISSUANCE, BUT RATHER A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) from industry that will allow the Government to identify commercial capabilities. The information sought herein is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a request for quote (RFQ), request for proposal (RFP), invitation for bid (IFB), or as an obligation or commitment on the part of the Government to acquire any product or service. There shall be no basis for claims against the Government as a result of information submitted in response to the RFI. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this RFI, or otherwise pay for any information submitted by respondents to this request. This notice is for market research purposes only and is not indicative of a full requirement. Any proposed items must meet or exceed the following specifications: Wearable Safety & Physiological Monitoring Technology Introduction & Objective The Government is conducting market research to identify commercially available, mature, and emerging technology solutions capable of enhancing the safety, accountability, and survivability of every Army Special Operations Forces (ARSOF) Soldier participating in Assessment, Selection, Qualification, and Professional Military Education (PME) courses. The Government seeks to understand industry capabilities, technical maturity, scalability, cost drivers, and risks associated with a wearable solution that provides real-time two-way communication, accurate location tracking, and continuous biometric monitoring viewable by cadre and safety personnel for safety management and risk mitigation. ARSOF training pipelines subject candidates to physically and mentally demanding conditions across varied terrain, climate, and duration. These conditions present inherent risks�including heat injury, cardiac events, dehydration, hypothermia, and physical incapacitation�that may occur outside the immediate observation of cadre. A technology-enabled safety monitoring capability is sought to enable early detection of physiological distress, rapid location of distressed personnel, and timely medical intervention. Technical Requirements & Capabilities To meet the requirements of this RFI, proposed systems should satisfy the following criteria. Respondents need not address every area but should clearly identify which capabilities they can provide. 1 Two-Way Communication Reliable two-way communication between wearer and cadre or safety personnel, allowing cadre to communicate with any selected user individually or the entire cohort simultaneously. Users may only communicate directly with cadre. Communication options include voice, data, or a combination of both. Wearer-initiated distress or man-down alert capability. Automated alerts sent to cadre when biometric thresholds are exceeded. Operation in degraded, denied, or no-infrastructure environments, such as mesh networks, satellite, or cellular fallback. 2 GPS / Location Services Near-real-time geolocation with desired accuracy of 10 meters or less and updates occurring every 30 seconds or less. Configurable and on-demand location updates. Geofencing with automated alerts when boundaries are departed. Reliable performance in GPS-degraded environments. Wearers must not be able to access location or time data from the device. Automated alerts at the control center when a unit remains stationary for preset periods as specified by cadre. 3 Biometric Monitoring Continuous monitoring of core body temperature, and heart rate at a minimum. Configurable, course-specific alert thresholds. Additional desirable parameters include respiration rate, hydration indicators, skin temperature, gate measurement, blood oxygen saturation (SpO?), and fall/impact detection. Monitoring equipment must not be constrictive, restrictive, or otherwise detracting from training. 4 Cadre Monitoring / Command Dashboard AI enabled to assess all data collected and provide warnings Centralized, simultaneous, real-time view of all monitored personnel (location, biometrics, alerts) Monitor 400+ devices per base station. Easy to use with minimal training. 24/7 Software Support for troubleshooting. Tiered alerting (visual/audible/push). Historical data logging and after-action analytics. 5 Hardware / Wearable Lightweight, low-profile design that does not restrict movement or blood flow for the wearer. Ruggedized construction with a target rating of IP67 or higher. Battery life sufficient for training events lasting over 24 hours, with rapid recharging capability. If reusable, must be easily sanitized. Must not interfere with other devices or wearers when in proximity. Waterproof up to 2 meters or greater. Audible distress beacon for rapid locating of wearers in crisis. 6 Cybersecurity & Data Approach to DoD RMF / Authority to Operate (ATO) per DoDI 8510.01. FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated encryption in transit and at rest. PHI/PII handling, role-based access, data ownership, and disposition. Information Requested from Industry- Interested vendors are requested to submit white papers or product data sheets, not to exceed 8 pages, detailing the following: Section A � Company Information 1. Company name, address, CAGE Code, UEI, and primary point of contact 2. Business size and socioeconomic status under the applicable NAICS code (e.g., small business, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, HUBZone) 3. Commercial and/or government customer base relevant to this capability Section B � Solution / Capability Description 1. Description of your solution and which capability areas it addresses 2. Technology Readiness Level (TRL) and current maturity (fielded, prototype, in development) 3. Demonstrated performance in austere, disconnected, or military environments 4. Known limitations, constraints, or accuracy/reliability considerations Section C � Cybersecurity & Data 1. Current ATO status or RMF experience within DoD; estimated timeline to achieve ATO if not already held 2. Approach to protecting PHI/PII, encryption, and data ownership/disposition Section D � Implementation & Sustainment 1. Scalability to support large cohorts and multiple geographically dispersed locations 2. Training, technical support, maintenance, warranty, and sustainment approach 3. Lead times for delivery, fielding, and standup Section E � Current Contracts 1. Existing contract vehicles through which the solution is available (e.g., GSA Schedule, SEWP, CSO/OTA eligibility, SBIR/STTR) Section F � Optional 1. Any additional information, innovations, or recommendations relevant to this requirement 2. Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost/pricing model (e.g., per-device, subscription, enterprise license) Documentation provided must address all required elements listed herein. Providing only a reference to a website is unacceptable for purposes of this announcement and will not be considered. All proprietary or corporate data received must be clearly identified. Do NOT submit classified material. Contractors interested in providing these supplies shall be registered in the System for Award Management (www.sam.gov). The Government makes no commitment to respond to questions submitted in response to this notice. No requests for capability briefings will be honored as a result of this notice. Information provided will not be used as a part of any subsequent solicitation requirement. No reimbursements will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement and/or any follow-up information requests. Failure to respond to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future associated requests for quotations that may be issued. Respondents will NOT be individually notified of the results. However, if the final determination results in the verification of a sole-source negotiation, a Notice of Intent to Sole Source and the redacted Justification and Approval will be posted to www.sam.gov.

title: Program Manager, Intelligence and Cyberspace Operations Maritime Targeting Cell Systems
description: General Announcement THIS NOTICE OF INTENT/SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATION PURPOSES ONLY. Program Manager, Intelligence and Cyberspace Operations (PM ICO) within Portfolio Acquisition Executive � Marine Corps (PAE-MC) provides this sources sought and notice of intent to award on a sole-source basis in accordance with 10 United States Code (U.S.C.) �3204 (a)(1), as implemented by the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-1(b) to Anduril Industries Inc., 1400 Anduril, Costa Mesa CA 92626-1548, CAGE: 85LD7, Unique Entity Identifier: KC3CH2MSK7Q3. The PMICO has a requirement for the procurement of fifteen (15) Maritime Targeting Cell (MTC) Shelter Systems, comprising (8) eight Operator Shelters and seven (7) Processing Shelters. These highly specialized, expeditionary, road-transportable, dual-shelter systems are required to support the urgent operational imperatives and timelines of the MTC program. These systems will provide a secure, self-contained, and ruggedized operating environment for conducting sensitive intelligence operations in contested and austere forward-deployed environments. 2. Basis for Sole-Source Justification Comprehensive market research was conducted across industry, including the evaluation of various vendor capability statements submitted in response to a previously posted Request for Information. Based on the responses received and technical analysis of market capabilities, the following was determined: Intended Source & Lack of Competition: Anduril Industries Inc. (1400 Anduril, Costa Mesa CA 92626-1548) is the only known source capable of satisfying the Government�s urgent operational requirements without unacceptable technical risk, cost duplication, and schedule delay. Competition is lacking because no other vendor possesses a mature, field-tested production configuration that provides turnkey integration with the Government-specified MEP-1070 generator set while concurrently meeting all expeditionary physical footprint, modularity, road-transportability, and operational security parameters. Technical & Integrated Architecture: The proprietary baseline developed by Anduril Industries provides pre-engineered structural, environmental, and tactical power integration with the required MEP-1070 generator set. This turnkey architecture is critical to minimizing the logistical footprint, ensuring rapid deployment, and significantly reducing setup time in austere, forward-operating environments. Programmatic & Schedule Impact: Alternative vendor concepts reviewed during market research would require extensive re-engineering, power integration/distribution redesign, and developmental qualification, to include environmental and flight/road-transport certifications. Pursuing an alternative development effort would introduce programmatic delays, creating an unacceptable operational gap in meeting mission-critical fleet deployment timelines for the MTC program. The Government anticipates award of a Firm-Fixed-Price delivery order, with a period of performance of approximately two (2) years. In tandem with executing this sole-source action and for all future opportunities, PM ICO will continue to conduct market research, monitor emerging industry capabilities, and actively pursue competitive acquisition strategies to the greatest extent practicable for future MTC program lifecycle and follow-on requirements. 3. Capability Statement Submission Instructions THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS OR QUOTATIONS. However, all responsible sources may submit a technical capability statement, proposal, or quotation demonstrating their ability to satisfy the Government's operational and technical requirements. The Government will not be responsible for any cost incurred in responding to this notice; however, interested parties may identify their interest and capability to meet the operational and technical requirements and past performance data no later than 12:00pm local time, Quantico, VA on 17 September 2026. Submissions received within 15 calendar days of this publication will be considered by the Government. Information received will be evaluated solely for determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All submissions shall become Government property and will not be returned. The North American Industry Classification System code is 541512, Computer Systems Design Services. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 7F20, IT and Telecom � IT Management Tool/Products (Hardware and Perpetual License Software). All responses to this notice shall be submitted to Mr. Jeffrey Newton at jeffrey.l.newton@usmc.mil and Ms. Brittney Moore at brittney.moore@usmc.mil. Please reference the notification identification number on all responses. Telephone calls will not be honored.

The contractor or site owner shall provide land use, access, infrastructure, and utilities necessary to support BLM-owned communications equipment and ensure uninterrupted radio communications services critical to employee safety and mission operations. Sole Source Contract Announcement This notice informs the public of BLM�s intent to award a sole source contract to provide land use, access, infrastructure and utilities necessary to support BLM-owned communications equipment and ensure uninterrupted radio communications services critical to employee safety and mission operations. The contract will be awarded in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 5.301(b)/5.101(b)(i) and will utilize Simplified Acquisition Procedures as authorized by RFO 6.103-1(b) under 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1). This statute authorizes sole source procurement when the property or services required are available only from one responsible source, or from a limited number of responsible sources, and no other type of property or services will satisfy the agency�s needs. The Snow Peak site is unique, geographically strategic location with existing infrastructure that supports field going personnel. No alternative sites in the vicinity meet the operational requirements due to the terrain and elevation of Snow Peak which provide critical connectivity. The existing infrastructure investments at this site would be cost-prohibitive to replicate elsewhere. title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Yole Inc
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE This is a notice of intent to award a sole source contract in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulations Overhaul (RFO) 12.102(a). Contracting Officers may solicit from one source if it's determined only one source is reasonably available to satisfy agency requirements, as supplemented with additional information in this notice. The U.S. Department of Commerce (DOC), Office of Acquisition Management (OAM), Shared Services Procurement Office (SSPO), located in Washington, D.C., intends to negotiate on a sole-source basis and award a contract to Yole Inc. on behalf of the International Trade Administration (ITA), Office of Industry & Analysis (I&A). This acquisition is being conducted under the authority of permitting other than full and open competition in accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 12.102 and in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 1901. This acquisition will result in a purchase order with a base 12-month period and one 12-month option period. DOC plans to issue a sole source purchase order to Yole for the acquisition of market intelligence reports covering key segments of the semiconductor and information and communications technology (ICT) industries. I&A requires specialized market intelligence to support OICT's responsibility to provide senior Department of Commerce officials, U.S. Government agencies, and U.S. firms with data, analyses, and recommendations concerning market trends within the semiconductor and ICT sectors. The required market intelligence supports OICT's analysis of technology trends, company market shares, global supply chains, U.S. industry competitiveness, export markets, and the development of effective trade policy. Yole Inc. is uniquely qualified to satisfy this requirement because the Government's requirement is for specifically identified proprietary Yole Group market intelligence publications and associated access to the Yole Group analysts responsible for the underlying research and analysis. The required reports are Yole Group products addressing specialized semiconductor markets, technologies, supply chains, and industry developments. As the publisher and owner of these proprietary market intelligence products, Yole controls the content, underlying research, methodologies, analyses, and associated analyst expertise incorporated into the required publications. The requirement cannot be satisfied merely through the acquisition of generalized semiconductors or ICT market research from another market research provider. OICT requires the specific Yole Group reports identified in the PWS, as well as direct consultation with relevant Yole Group analysts to clarify and provide context regarding the information contained in those reports. Other market research companies may offer research concerning similar industries or technologies; however, those products would contain independently developed datasets, methodologies, forecasts, market segmentation, and analyses and would therefore not provide the specific Yole research products required by OICT. Accordingly, Yole Inc. is the only source reasonably capable of providing the specific proprietary publications and associated Yole analyst consultations required to meet the Government's stated need. Award to another source would not provide the Government with the required Yole Group research and analyst access. Therefore, use of the sole-source authority provided by RFO 12.102 is appropriate for this acquisition. title: Wearable Safety & Physiological Monitoring Technology
description: THIS IS NOT A NOTICE OF SOLICITATION ISSUANCE, BUT RATHER A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) from industry that will allow the Government to identify commercial capabilities. The information sought herein is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a request for quote (RFQ), request for proposal (RFP), invitation for bid (IFB), or as an obligation or commitment on the part of the Government to acquire any product or service. There shall be no basis for claims against the Government as a result of information submitted in response to the RFI. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this RFI, or otherwise pay for any information submitted by respondents to this request. This notice is for market research purposes only and is not indicative of a full requirement. Any proposed items must meet or exceed the following specifications: Wearable Safety & Physiological Monitoring Technology Introduction & Objective The Government is conducting market research to identify commercially available, mature, and emerging technology solutions capable of enhancing the safety, accountability, and survivability of every Army Special Operations Forces (ARSOF) Soldier participating in Assessment, Selection, Qualification, and Professional Military Education (PME) courses. The Government seeks to understand industry capabilities, technical maturity, scalability, cost drivers, and risks associated with a wearable solution that provides real-time two-way communication, accurate location tracking, and continuous biometric monitoring viewable by cadre and safety personnel for safety management and risk mitigation. ARSOF training pipelines subject candidates to physically and mentally demanding conditions across varied terrain, climate, and duration. These conditions present inherent risks�including heat injury, cardiac events, dehydration, hypothermia, and physical incapacitation�that may occur outside the immediate observation of cadre. A technology-enabled safety monitoring capability is sought to enable early detection of physiological distress, rapid location of distressed personnel, and timely medical intervention. Technical Requirements & Capabilities To meet the requirements of this RFI, proposed systems should satisfy the following criteria. Respondents need not address every area but should clearly identify which capabilities they can provide. 1 Two-Way Communication Reliable two-way communication between wearer and cadre or safety personnel, allowing cadre to communicate with any selected user individually or the entire cohort simultaneously. Users may only communicate directly with cadre. Communication options include voice, data, or a combination of both. Wearer-initiated distress or man-down alert capability. Automated alerts sent to cadre when biometric thresholds are exceeded. Operation in degraded, denied, or no-infrastructure environments, such as mesh networks, satellite, or cellular fallback. 2 GPS / Location Services Near-real-time geolocation with desired accuracy of 10 meters or less and updates occurring every 30 seconds or less. Configurable and on-demand location updates. Geofencing with automated alerts when boundaries are departed. Reliable performance in GPS-degraded environments. Wearers must not be able to access location or time data from the device. Automated alerts at the control center when a unit remains stationary for preset periods as specified by cadre. 3 Biometric Monitoring Continuous monitoring of core body temperature, and heart rate at a minimum. Configurable, course-specific alert thresholds. Additional desirable parameters include respiration rate, hydration indicators, skin temperature, gate measurement, blood oxygen saturation (SpO?), and fall/impact detection. Monitoring equipment must not be constrictive, restrictive, or otherwise detracting from training. 4 Cadre Monitoring / Command Dashboard AI enabled to assess all data collected and provide warnings Centralized, simultaneous, real-time view of all monitored personnel (location, biometrics, alerts) Monitor 400+ devices per base station. Easy to use with minimal training. 24/7 Software Support for troubleshooting. Tiered alerting (visual/audible/push). Historical data logging and after-action analytics. 5 Hardware / Wearable Lightweight, low-profile design that does not restrict movement or blood flow for the wearer. Ruggedized construction with a target rating of IP67 or higher. Battery life sufficient for training events lasting over 24 hours, with rapid recharging capability. If reusable, must be easily sanitized. Must not interfere with other devices or wearers when in proximity. Waterproof up to 2 meters or greater. Audible distress beacon for rapid locating of wearers in crisis. 6 Cybersecurity & Data Approach to DoD RMF / Authority to Operate (ATO) per DoDI 8510.01. FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated encryption in transit and at rest. PHI/PII handling, role-based access, data ownership, and disposition. Information Requested from Industry- Interested vendors are requested to submit white papers or product data sheets, not to exceed 8 pages, detailing the following: Section A � Company Information 1. Company name, address, CAGE Code, UEI, and primary point of contact 2. Business size and socioeconomic status under the applicable NAICS code (e.g., small business, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, HUBZone) 3. Commercial and/or government customer base relevant to this capability Section B � Solution / Capability Description 1. Description of your solution and which capability areas it addresses 2. Technology Readiness Level (TRL) and current maturity (fielded, prototype, in development) 3. Demonstrated performance in austere, disconnected, or military environments 4. Known limitations, constraints, or accuracy/reliability considerations Section C � Cybersecurity & Data 1. Current ATO status or RMF experience within DoD; estimated timeline to achieve ATO if not already held 2. Approach to protecting PHI/PII, encryption, and data ownership/disposition Section D � Implementation & Sustainment 1. Scalability to support large cohorts and multiple geographically dispersed locations 2. Training, technical support, maintenance, warranty, and sustainment approach 3. Lead times for delivery, fielding, and standup Section E � Current Contracts 1. Existing contract vehicles through which the solution is available (e.g., GSA Schedule, SEWP, CSO/OTA eligibility, SBIR/STTR) Section F � Optional 1. Any additional information, innovations, or recommendations relevant to this requirement 2. Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost/pricing model (e.g., per-device, subscription, enterprise license) Documentation provided must address all required elements listed herein. Providing only a reference to a website is unacceptable for purposes of this announcement and will not be considered. All proprietary or corporate data received must be clearly identified. Do NOT submit classified material. Contractors interested in providing these supplies shall be registered in the System for Award Management (www.sam.gov). The Government makes no commitment to respond to questions submitted in response to this notice. No requests for capability briefings will be honored as a result of this notice. Information provided will not be used as a part of any subsequent solicitation requirement. No reimbursements will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement and/or any follow-up information requests. Failure to respond to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future associated requests for quotations that may be issued. Respondents will NOT be individually notified of the results. However, if the final determination results in the verification of a sole-source negotiation, a Notice of Intent to Sole Source and the redacted Justification and Approval will be posted to www.sam.gov.
