title: Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation System - Indianapolis VAMC
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) subpart 12.202, �Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Products and Commercial Services,� as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a written solicitation document will not be issued. This solicitation RFQ- 36C25026Q1013 is issued as a request for quote (RFQ). This solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01, effective 03/13/2026. This is a firm fixed price, Small Business Set-Aside solicitation. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) number is 334510. NOTE: This solicitation is for one Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation System that is FDA-cleared for Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). All interested companies shall provide quotations for the requirements listed below. Materials and parts will be delivered to: Richard L. Roudebush VA Medical Center, 1481 W. 10th St., Indianapolis, IN 46202, FOB destination. Minimum Requirements The required TMS device must have the following salient characteristics, specific to the clinical needs and operation at our VAMC: - Delivers a series of pulsed magnetic stimuli to targeted regions of the brain, following predefined treatment protocols. - Non-invasive procedure�requires no anesthesia and does not disrupt normal cognitive functions. - Flat purchase model: No pay-per-use fees; acquisition includes all treatment protocols. - Upgradeable treatment protocols: Device must support future protocol updates. - High patient throughput: Utilizes a liquid-cooled TMS coil for sustained clinical use with minimal downtime. - Low acoustic noise: Device operates at low intensity acoustic signature (clicking), minimizing patient discomfort. - System adaptable to any practice size: Must be installable in a variety of clinical settings. - Theraburst stimulation capability as an available therapy option. - Clinical safety and efficacy: Free from common antidepressant side effects (weight gain, sexual dysfunction). - Onsite installation and training: Contractor provides initial setup and hands-on orientation for clinical staff. - Ongoing technical and marketing support included. - Comprehensive documentation and warranty: Delivered with product documentation, warranty information, and support contacts. TMS device is being used to treat: - Major Depressive Disorder (MDD): Specifically for patients who have not responded to at least one antidepressant medication. - Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD): FDA-cleared protocols for OCD treatment are also utilized. The goal is to provide safe, evidence-based neurostimulation for refractory depression and OCD, improving patient outcomes where conventional pharmacologic treatments have failed or are not tolerated. Contact: Rachel MacRae, Contracting Specialist, via email at rachel.macrae@va.gov. No telephone inquiries will be accepted. Only written inquiries received directly for the offeror are acceptable. All quotes must be received by 9/17/2026 by 12:00pm EST to Rachel MacRae (rachel.macrae@va.gov). Offerors must comply with all instructions contained in provision 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors- Commercial Products (SEP 2023) (DEVIATION OCT 2025), applying to this acquisition. An award will be based upon a comparative evaluation of quotes in accordance with the Simplified Acquisition Procedures of RFO FAR 12. Comparative evaluation is the side by side pairwise comparison of quotes based on factors resulting in a Contracting Officer decision for the quote most favorable to the Government. The following must be completed to be considered for award: - Quote with the following information o The solicitation number; o The name, address, telephone number of the Offeror; o The Offeror�s Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and, if applicable, Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) indicator;o A technical description of the items being offered in sufficient detail to evaluate compliance with the requirements in the solicitation. This may include product literature, or other documents, if necessary; - FAR 52.225-2 � Buy American Certificate (see attached) - Offerors must complete annual representations and certifications electronically via the System for Award Management (SAM) website located at https://sam.gov. - To facilitate the award process, all quotes must include a statement regarding the terms and conditions herein as follows: �The terms and conditions in the solicitation are acceptable to be included in the award document without modification, deletion, or addition.� OR �The terms and conditions in the solicitation are acceptable to be included in the award document with the exception, deletion, or addition of the following:" Quoters shall list exception(s) and rationale for the exception(s), if any. Contractor shall provide an authorized distribution letter. The Contractor shall be an Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) authorized dealer, authorized distributor, or authorized Contractor reseller for the proposed equipment/system such that the OEM warranty and service are provided and maintained by the OEM. All warranty and service associated with the equipment/system shall be in accordance with the OEM terms and conditions. The Contractor shall provide new items ONLY; no remanufactured/used or "gray market" items (852.212-71 Gray Market and Counterfeit Items (FEB 2023)). All items must be covered by the manufacturer's warranty.

title: K-12 Newcomer Curriculum and Customization Services for ORR
description: Amendment 1: The purpose of this amendment is to: Extend the response due date to September 17, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time (ET); and Invite industry representatives to participate in a roundtable discussion with the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) to further discuss the requirement and provide industry feedback. Information regarding the roundtable discussion, including registration instructions, is provided in the PowerPoint presentation located in the Attachments/Links section of this notice. Objective: The Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) is conducting market research to identify qualified contractors capable of providing a commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) K-12 educational curriculum tailored for newcomer and migrant students, along with professional services to customize the material to fit specific regional, demographic, and compliance requirements. The curriculum model should include child assessments (initial assessment, assessment every 30 days, and an exit assessment). The curriculum model shall be trauma informed and integrate social emotional learning; and be customizable to the different ORR funded residential care programs such as shelters, secure care, long-term foster care, therapeutic care sites, and a potential home-schooling model. Background and Target Population: The target student population consist of K-12 newcomers, immigrant children, and migrant youth. These students often present unique educational needs including: Varying levels of English Language Proficiency (ELP), including students with Interrupted Formal Education (SIFE). A critical need for rapid acculturation, social-emotional learning (SEL) support, foundational literacy/numeracy, including trauma informed teaching strategies and guidance. Highly transient lifestyles requiring flexible, modular learning units. Scope of Work: The selected contractor shall deliver a comprehensive solution consisting of both curriculum materials and instructional design customization services; including professional services contractors to support ORR headquarters with successful implementation and monitoring of K-12 curriculum for newcomers in all ORR funded residential and care programs for unaccompanied alien children (UAC), as well as providing ORR funded program teaching staff with training and technical assistance. It shall include child assessments (initial assessment, assessment every 30 days, and an exit assessment), and be trauma informed and integrate social emotional learning.

title: Program Manager, Intelligence and Cyberspace Operations Maritime Targeting Cell Systems
description: General Announcement THIS NOTICE OF INTENT/SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATION PURPOSES ONLY. Program Manager, Intelligence and Cyberspace Operations (PM ICO) within Portfolio Acquisition Executive � Marine Corps (PAE-MC) provides this sources sought and notice of intent to award on a sole-source basis in accordance with 10 United States Code (U.S.C.) �3204 (a)(1), as implemented by the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-1(b) to Anduril Industries Inc., 1400 Anduril, Costa Mesa CA 92626-1548, CAGE: 85LD7, Unique Entity Identifier: KC3CH2MSK7Q3. The PMICO has a requirement for the procurement of fifteen (15) Maritime Targeting Cell (MTC) Shelter Systems, comprising (8) eight Operator Shelters and seven (7) Processing Shelters. These highly specialized, expeditionary, road-transportable, dual-shelter systems are required to support the urgent operational imperatives and timelines of the MTC program. These systems will provide a secure, self-contained, and ruggedized operating environment for conducting sensitive intelligence operations in contested and austere forward-deployed environments. Basis for Sole-Source Justification Comprehensive market research was conducted across industry, including the evaluation of various vendor capability statements submitted in response to a previously posted Request for Information. Based on the responses received and technical analysis of market capabilities, the following was determined: Intended Source & Lack of Competition: Anduril Industries Inc. (1400 Anduril, Costa Mesa CA 92626-1548) is the only known source capable of satisfying the Government�s urgent operational requirements without unacceptable technical risk, cost duplication, and schedule delay. Competition is lacking because no other vendor possesses a mature, field-tested production configuration that provides turnkey integration with the Government-specified MEP-1070 generator set while concurrently meeting all expeditionary physical footprint, modularity, road-transportability, and operational security parameters. Technical & Integrated Architecture: The proprietary baseline developed by Anduril Industries provides pre-engineered structural, environmental, and tactical power integration with the required MEP-1070 generator set. This turnkey architecture is critical to minimizing the logistical footprint, ensuring rapid deployment, and significantly reducing setup time in austere, forward-operating environments. Programmatic & Schedule Impact: Alternative vendor concepts reviewed during market research would require extensive re-engineering, power integration/distribution redesign, and developmental qualification, to include environmental and flight/road-transport certifications. Pursuing an alternative development effort would introduce programmatic delays, creating an unacceptable operational gap in meeting mission-critical fleet deployment timelines for the MTC program. The Government anticipates award of a Firm-Fixed-Price delivery order, with a period of performance of approximately two (2) years. In tandem with executing this sole-source action and for all future opportunities, PM ICO will continue to conduct market research, monitor emerging industry capabilities, and actively pursue competitive acquisition strategies to the greatest extent practicable for future MTC program lifecycle and follow-on requirements. Capability Statement Submission Instructions THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS OR QUOTATIONS. However, all responsible sources may submit a technical capability statement, proposal, or quotation demonstrating their ability to satisfy the Government's operational and technical requirements. The Government will not be responsible for any cost incurred in responding to this notice; however, interested parties may identify their interest and capability to meet the operational and technical requirements and past performance data no later than 12:00pm local time, Quantico, VA on 17 September 2026. Submissions received within 15 calendar days of this publication will be considered by the Government. Information received will be evaluated solely for determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All submissions shall become Government property and will not be returned. The North American Industry Classification System code is 541512, Computer Systems Design Services. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 7F20, IT and Telecom � IT Management Tool/Products (Hardware and Perpetual License Software). All responses to this notice shall be submitted to Mr. Jeffrey Newton at jeffrey.l.newton@usmc.mil and Ms. Brittney Moore at brittney.moore@usmc.mil. Please reference the notification identification number on all responses. Telephone calls will not be honored.

title: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract - Parking Garage Services
description: 1. Action Description The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) intends to award a sole-source firm-fixed-price contract to Arlington VA I FGF LLC, Chicago IL, the owner and lessor of the property located at 675 N. Randolph Street in Arlington, Virginia, to provide secure, controlled parking and related facility support services for the below-grade structed parking garage directly beneath DARPA Headquarters. 2. Background and Scope of Services DARPA requires continued control of the below-grade structured parking garage located at 675 N. Randolph Street. The garage is physically integrated with and located directly beneath the DARPA Headquarters facility. The Contractor will be required to provide comprehensive facility support services necessary to maintain the garage in a safe, operational, and secure condition. These services may include structural maintenance; mechanical, ventilation, and related building system support; fire and life-safety system support; emergency infrastructure support; compliance with Department of War below-grade, structured parking garage at 675 North Randolph Street, Arlington, VA, to ensure a fully secure and operational exclusive-use parking facility for DARPA. Historically, parking and associated access-control capabilities were included within the master building lease managed by Washington Headquarters Services (WHS). As a result of changes to the WHS leasing structure, these requirements will no longer be included in the master lease. Therefore, DARPA intends to independently procure the services necessary to maintain control of the below-grade parking area and support the physical-security requirements of its headquarters facility. 3. Authority and Basis for the Proposed Sole Source Acquisition This proposed acquisition is being conducted under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(1) (formerly 10 U.S.C. � 2304(c)(1)), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, "Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements." DARPA�s market research identified numerous commercial parking facilities in Arlington, Virginia that can provide general commercial parking. However, the Government has not identified an alternative facility capable of satisfying all of the following requirements: Unique Physical Location and Integration. The required parking facility is physically integrated with and located directly beneath DARPA Headquarters at 675 N. Randolph Street. No other commercial parking facility can provide the same physical relationship to the DARPA facility. Physical Security and Access Control. DARPA requires controlled vehicle access to the below-grade parking area to support the physical security requirements applicable to the Agency headquarters facility. For instance, in accordance with Department of Defense (currently Department of War (DoW)) Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) 4-010-01 (DoD Minimum Antiterrorism Standards for Buildings), access control to subterranean structures directly beneath DoW offices is a critical security vulnerability. Proprietary Rights and Building Systems. The Government requires access to the garage and the building systems integral to its operation, including structural, ventilation, mechanical, and fire and life safety systems that support the garage. Arlington VA I FGF, LLC owns and controls the property where the garage facility is located. Because those rights and systems are controlled by the property owner, another source could not independently provide the Government with exclusive rights to the same facility without authorization from the owner. Continuity of Operations. DARPA requires a transition that does not create an interruption in the physical security and access control measures supporting DARPA Headquarters. 4. Determination DARPA has determined that Arlington VA I FGF, LLC is the only responsible source capable of providing the required services, and no other type of services will satisfy all the Agency�s requirements because: The Government�s requirement extends beyond obtaining parking spaces in the Arlington, Virgina area. An alternative, off-site parking facility would not provide the Government with control of the area directly beneath DARPA Headquarters or eliminate the Government�s continuing requirement to maintain appropriate physical security controls over that area. Unrestricted or uncontrolled commercial use of the area directly beneath the headquarters could adversely affect the physical-security posture of the facility. Maintaining the existing below-grade parking facility avoids the operational and security disruption that could result from attempting to relocate the parking function while simultaneously maintaining control of the area directly beneath the headquarters. 5. Notice to Interested Sources This notice is not a request for competitive proposals. It is issued to determine whether any responsible sources can demonstrate their capability to satisfy the Government�s complete requirement and provide a basis for the Government to reconsider the contemplated sole-source acquisition. Interested sources are invited to submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation demonstration, with objective and specific information, their ability to satisfy all of the Government�s requirements. The ability to provide ordinary commercial parking spaces at another Arlington, Virginia location, standing alone, will not satisfy the requirement. A response should address, at a minimum, the following: Physical and Legal Access. Legal authority and practical ability to obtain the rights necessary to provide exclusive and controlled use of, and perform the required services within, the below-grade parking facility directly beneath 675 North Randolph Street in Arlington, Virginia. Security and Access Control. Ability to satisfy the Government�s physical security and controlled access requirements applicable to the below-grade parking facility, including applicable Department of War requirements, such as compliance with DoD Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) 4-010-01 for subterranean facility access control. Continuity of Operations. Ability to provide uninterrupted services during transition and throughout contract performance without compromising DARPA�s physical security requirements. Organizational Capability. Identify relevant experience, technical capabilities, facilities, personnel, and other resources demonstrating ability to perform the required services. System for Award Management (SAM) Registration. Provide documentation of current registration in SAM, including a valid Unique Entity ID (UEI) and CAGE code, as applicable. Interested sources should submit a capability statement addressing the requirements identified above to the Primary and Secondary points of contact listed above no later than the Response Deadline. Generic statements of interest or statements that merely demonstrate an ability to provide commercial parking services will not be sufficient. The Government will consider all timely and substantive responses solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete the contemplated contract action, based on responses to this notice or otherwise, will be within the Government�s discretion and consistent with applicable acquisition laws and regulations. The Government is not responsible for costs incurred by interested sources in preparing or submitting responses to this notice.

description: Solicitation Amendment #1 The purpose of this amendment is to resolve a discrepancy in the original solicitation notice regarding the SOW technical specifications and to formally extend the quotation submission deadline. The Government is amending the solicitation to clarify the submission requirements and ensure all potential offerors are quoting against the correct technical parameters. Summary of Changes: Equipment Baseline Correction: The original SOW contained conflicting baseline specifications regarding the fan motor horsepower and low-speed operational thresholds. Based on detailed technical verification, the following corrections have been made: The SOW has been updated to reflect the correct 10HP motor requirement (superseding the previously noted 2.5HP reference). Responses will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy, including whether a set-aside is appropriate. The anticipated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 561320, Temporary Help Services. Respondents may identify other NAICS codes they believe are more appropriate to the requirement, such as those applicable to offices of physicians or mental health specialists. 1.0 BACKGROUND The Great Plains Area Office (GPAO) works in conjunction with its 19 Indian Health Service Units and Tribal Managed Service Units to provide health care to approximately 122,000 Native Americans located in North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, and Iowa. The Area Office�s service units include seven hospitals, eight health centers, and several smaller health stations and satellite clinics. IHS anticipates providing 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, 365 days per year (24/7/365) synchronous audio-video telebehavioral health services in support of Emergency Department (ED) operations at facilities within the Great Plains Area. 2.0 OBJECTIVE The mission of the Indian Health Service is to raise the physical, mental, social, and spiritual health of American Indians and Alaska Natives to the highest level. As part of this mission, IHS is committed to ensuring the safety and security of its patients, staff, and facilities while providing high-quality health care services across its regions. The purpose of this requirement is to provide services to patients presenting to Emergency Departments with suicide attempts, acute psychiatric crises, substance-related emergencies, and co-occurring disorders. Timely behavioral health assessment and intervention are critical to patient safety, regulatory compliance, and appropriate disposition. 3.0 SCOPE The Contractor shall provide qualified, licensed independent behavioral health clinicians, including psychologists, psychiatrists, Licensed Clinical Social Workers (LCSWs), Licensed Professional Counselors-Mental Health (LPC-MHs), or equivalent professionals, to deliver real-time telebehavioral health services. Services shall include, as clinically indicated and/or required by facility workflows: Suicide risk assessment and completion of the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) with Suicide Assessment Five-Step Evaluation and Triage (SAFE-T) for patients presenting with suicidal ideation or suicide attempts. Crisis intervention, de-escalation guidance, and reassessment as indicated. Individualized Stanley-Brown Safety Planning, including lethal means counseling when appropriate. Placement coordination for patients requiring higher levels of care, including inpatient psychiatric care, crisis stabilization, and detoxification services, with documentation of placement attempts. Language-access coordination, including telephonic, video remote interpreting (VRI), and American Sign Language (ASL) interpreter services available within 15 minutes of request and documented in the Electronic Health Record (EHR). Culturally responsive and trauma-informed care, supported by annual clinician training in areas such as cultural competency, implicit bias, and trauma-informed care. For patients presenting with acute psychiatric crises, qualified prescribing providers�including psychiatrists, psychiatric nurse practitioners, or psychologists with prescribing privileges�shall be available to consult with the ED provider regarding appropriate medication stabilization. Prior to initiation of a consultation, the Contractor shall receive a report from the referring provider or designee. At the conclusion of the patient evaluation, the telebehavioral health provider shall provide a report to the referring provider or designee. 4.0 CONTRACT REQUIREMENTS AND PERSONNEL QUALIFICATIONS The Contractor shall maintain sufficient qualified personnel and operational capacity to provide the required synchronous audio-video telebehavioral health coverage 24/7/365, including weekends and Federal holidays. Personnel shall possess the professional qualifications, licensure, credentials, and prescribing authority, as applicable, necessary to perform the services described in this notice. 5.0 TYPE OF ORDER The anticipated award is a firm-fixed-price, performance-based acquisition purchase order. 6.0 ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE The anticipated period of performance is a Base Period plus Four Option Years, as follows: Base Period: August 1, 2027 � July 31, 2028 Option Year 1: August 1, 2028 � July 31, 2029 Option Year 2: August 1, 2029 � July 31, 2030 Option Year 3: August 1, 2030 � July 31, 2031 Option Year 4: August 1, 2031 � July 31, 2032 7.0 PLACE OF PERFORMANCE The requirement supports facilities within the Great Plains Area, Indian Health Service. title: FY 26 - FY 31 Unaccompanied Housing Wi-Fi
description: 14th Contracting Squadron located at Columbus AFB, MS 39710, intends to award a sole source award to Cable One INC/ dba Spraklight, 606 Noble Street, Anniston, Alabama 36201. This requirement is for a turnkey solution to engineer, furnish, install, test, and maintain a commercial wireless internet (Wi-Fi) service for the unaccompanied housing dormitories and designated common areas at Columbus Air Force Base (CAFB), MS. The objective is to deliver reliable, high-speed Internet access to all residents at no cost to them, in compliance with all Department of the Air Force policies. The purpose of this service is to provide Dorm Wireless Internet to 3-day rooms, 94 dorm rooms, and 3 outdoor pavilions postured on one campus at Columbus Air Force Base (AFB). The contractor shall provide installation and all necessary equipment, to include up to 73 modems, up to two WI-FI repeaters and up to seven 24 port switches as specified in the Statement of Work (SOW) for a period of five years one (1) Base Year of 12 months and four (4) 12-month option years. Additionally, for Wide Area WorkFlow (WAWF) invoicing, the BPN for both the Inspector and the Acceptor is F1N3BA; no separate inspector is necessary. The Government intends to acquire this commercial service under FAR Part 12 and to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1 and DFARS 206.302-1. The proposed source is Cable One INC/ dba Spraklight . Based on the facts documented in the justification, only this source can meet the Government�s requirement because Sparklight (Cable One, Inc.) is currently the only internet service provider with existing cable infrastructure on Columbus Air Force Base capable of providing the required dormitory wireless internet service to the UEQ campus. Other potential carriers do not currently have the necessary on-site infrastructure and equipment and have not obtained the installation franchise agreement required to provide internet service on the installation. This is not a request for competitive proposals, quotations, or offers. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation that will be considered by the Government. Interested sources shall demonstrate their capability to provide a turnkey dormitory Wi-Fi solution that meets the Government�s requirements, including engineering, furnishing, installation, testing, sustainment, continuity of resident service, interoperability with existing infrastructure as applicable, licensing, and all other requirements identified in the attached public-release SOW/PWS. The Government will evaluate timely responses to determine whether another source can meet the requirement and whether a competitive procurement is warranted. Responses must contain sufficient detail for the Government to assess the source�s technical capability and transition approach. Submit responses through the contact method identified in the SAM.gov notice no later than the stated response deadline. Capability statements and related materials must be e-mailed to Brownlee, John M at john.brownlee.2@us.af.mil and Booth, Dylan L at dylan.booth.1@us.af.mil by 12:00 PM Central Daylight Time on 17th September 2026.
